utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Please be seated. Good afternoon to everybody. May we hear the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon. Case Number IT-97-24-T, the Prosecutor versus Milomir Stakic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. And the appearances, for the Prosecution, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, Joanna Korner, Nicholas Koumjian, assisted by Ruth Karper, case manager. Good afternoon, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: For the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Branko Lukic and Danilo Cirkovic for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. Before we start, we have no doubt to discuss the -- let's call it last-minute request by the Defence we received late Friday evening. Let me take the opportunity to tell the Defence that in future, we can't accept such late requests, leaving no possibility at all for the Chamber having heard the OTP to decide responsibly on these questions. You knew beforehand, since the end of last year - I think it was the beginning of December - that Mr. Sivac would be here this week. And therefore, I think it has nothing to do a fair approach vis-a-vis the other party and the Bench to come with such an important document on a last-minute basis. But let us hear the remarks by the Prosecution, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, first of all may I explain the situation in respect Mr. Sivac. He testified this morning and is still required to return tomorrow for cross-examination, further cross-examination. I've spoken to Defence counsel, Mr. Ackerman, and he has no objection if Your Honours rule it right for Mr. Sivac to testify here this afternoon even though he is effectively still testifying in the other case. And the other matter is, we understand from him, that he is obliged by business commits to leave by midday tomorrow. So if Your Honours do allow him to testify, it should be this afternoon. Your Honour, in respect of the proposed questions, Your Honour, the first two are simply a repetition of his evidence. Three, four, and five, Your Honour, really depend on what Your Honours' view is, in our submission, of the following questions. Your Honour, they have already put -- question six, they have already put to Mr. Sivac that he is wrong, mistaken, lying about having seen Mr. Stakic as part of the delegation. It is in our submission an improper form of question because it's nothing more than a comment to say to the witness "What do you say to the fact that Srdjo Srdic unequivocally and emphatically states that he never visited the camps and further denies ever visiting Omarska Detention Centre?" First of all, Srdjo Srdic hasn't said that to the Court; he said that in interview with the Office of the Prosecutor. So it's in evidence of what he told the Office of Prosecutor. And secondly, and I know that Your Honours' have already made it clear that you don't approve of this form of cross-examination, cross-examination should be putting the case for the defendant plus facts. It is not, as I say, proper to say "A witness says that you're wrong. What do you say to that"? That's just inviting comment. Your Honour, it is equally improper to put to him that Mr. Srdic is a liar and cannot be trusted. That is a matter of opinion and not proper. Question number eight, "Is it your position that Srdjo Srdic would deny things and blame others only to save himself?" He is being invited to comment upon the character of a person who is not yet in any shape or form a witness. But as I say, Your Honour, all of these depend on whether Your Honours think that question xis is a proper question, and we say it is not. They have firmly put their case. Nobody can be in any doubt about it, neither Your Honours nor the Office of the Prosecutor. The proper way of dealing with it is to call Srdjo Srdic to testify that Stakic never visited Omarska. Your Honour, I utterly fail to understand of what relevance the questions in respect of the Red Cross can be. Question number two is the same objection as to question number six. "What do you say, sir, to the fact that Srdjo Srdic contends that he always cautioned the Red Cross representatives?" What is he supposed to say? I mean, it's a rhetorical question, Your Honour. But two things: All he can say is "I don't know one way or the other." Or if he did, that's not what happened. But in any event, as I say, I maintain my objection that that's an improper form of cross-examination. Then the later ones about the Red Cross. Now, Your Honour, I'm at somewhat of a difficulty here, and I forgot to check with Mr. Koumjian. I don't know whether or not questions were already asked about the Red Cross to Mr. Sivac. But unless it is alleged that this is brand-new information that the Defence were unaware of before they received the interview of Mr. Srdic, and these are all matters which have been put to Mr. Sivac when he was here giving testimony originally and, Your Honour, because I'm reminded that the interview took place in August, and he testified in July. Your Honour, question number five under that second section: "It is your position that Srdjo Srdic is also lying about the responsibility?" Again, we raise the same objection. And then question number 8: "Do you know if it's true or not that Srdjo Srdic personally profited from his position at the Red Cross?" I'm sorry, Your Honour, I utterly fail to see what conceivable relevance that has to any issue that Your Honours have to decide in this case. So, Your Honour, the upshot is this: We object to any form of questioning that relates to it being put in the form that "Srdjo Srdic has said this; what do you say about that," and anything which were matters that were known to the Defence before and which they could have put at the time when Mr. Sivac testified originally. Your Honour, in respect of the second -- item c on this request, it starts, "Sir, since your last testimony in July 2002, we have come to learn that you suffer from various medical conditions." Your Honour, firstly, I don't know whether that may be correct; it may not be correct. Second, we've had no notice of any documentation in relation to his medical condition. We certainly don't know what the answers to these questions are. And third, if it is right, to what issue in the case is it suggested these questions go?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: The Defence may answer if they so want.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. First of all, I would say again that we wouldn't have to cross-examine Mr. Sivac again if the Prosecution disclosed what they had to disclose to us in a timely manner. Now --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Sorry, can you explain this sentence to me. The hearing by the Prosecution took place in August, and we heard Mr. Sivac in July. How can you come to this statement?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If we had at that time the statements --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: We couldn't have the statement. The statement was taken later.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If we had the statements of these six persons

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: situation. But --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Sorry. Aren't you aware that the testimony of Mr. Srdic apparently was taken in August 2002?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Sorry. Then -- I'm sorry, Your Honour. You are right. I was thinking about the five other witnesses. But your guideline to us was to question this witness, if he appears again, only related to the statement of the witnesses, to the statements of the witnesses - we know which six witnesses; I don't want to mention their names. So we tried to restrain ourselves only to the statements of those six witnesses. And specifically, we found very interesting the statement of Mr. Srdjo Srdic who spoke differently than Mr. Sivac is claiming. And we think that we have the right to impeach any witness if it's not our witness. And maybe, this is our attempt to impeach Mr. Srdic through Mr. Sivac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. I think we shouldn't go into far more details. We should find a pragmatic solution. Mr. Sivac is present here today. And I think the only point with some merits - we discussed it previously together, the Bench - is that Mr. Srdic stated in this interview of August 2002 that he never visited camps, which might be a contradiction to the statement of Mr. Sivac. But at the same time, there seem to be slight, but I emphasise only slight, discrepancies which are easy to understand after ten years with the testimony of Madam Markovska last week. So instead of waiting until the end of the case and maybe then during rejoinder or rebuttal or ex officio by the Judges to come to final clarification on these points, I think it would be the best to reopen the case, which of course, and the Defence has to know this, gives another opportunity also to put additional questions to this witness, and then to reopen the cross-examination, and then we -- I think we have the best and most practical solution immediately today.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, can I make this absolutely clear, and then Mr. Lukic can address you again. The only aspect on which you're allowing further cross-examination of Mr. Sivac is on the basis that Srdic says that Stakic never visited the camps?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: In principle, yes. Only to balance the right to put questions to the witness, is that I learned by the senior legal officer today that there would additional questions put to the witness by you. This, of course, would give the possibility to the Defence from their side to put other questions not limited to these in the framework of an honourary cross-examination to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. We were only going to do it if Your Honours allowed it to be recalled, but he has brought further articles with him. But Your Honour, my concern is simply this: It is perfectly proper to say to the witness, for example, "Do you know Mr. Srdic? Do you know he's an honest man? Tell us what you know about his reputation," and then to go on to say -- to repeat the cross-examination, in other words, "Mr. Sivac, do you still stick to your answer that Stakic visited Omarska?" But, Your Honour, I do maintain my objection to the form of the question. "What do you say to the fact that Srdjo Srdic unequivocally and emphatically states that he never visited the camp?" One, we don't know that's what Mr. Srdic may or may not say if he gives evidence; and two, it is inviting the witness to comment. The proper way of putting a question like this is you can certainly ask if there's any reason to believe whether Mr. Srdic would lie or anything like that, but it is not to put the question in that form.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I believe the Defence has understood the message, and it will be rephrased in an appropriate way. And related to the medical background, I think this was already covered; the points related to Red Cross, I can't see the relevance to our concrete case. And so it would be relatively limited. And I think it would be only fair that the questions to Mr. Sivac would be put to him on the basis of, as we did it last week with Madam Markovska, on the basis of this video. I think it was S22. I'm not quite sure in the moment.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: J22, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: J22, okay. J22. And then in addition, the former -- I don't think it was a sketch at that time. I think it was Exhibit S52-1, that we restart from that point where Mr. Sivac marked where the delegation from his point of view and at that time his best recollection, where the delegation arrived and where the prisoners were lined up and where the delegation went into the offices. So then we can at the same time have a clarification opposed to the testimony of Madam Markovska.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: We should proceed this way without further ado because it's the most practical exercise.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: There has to be further review for this reason. I'm sorry. Mr. Sivac only finished testifying at 10 minutes to 2.00, so he was taken off to have some lunch and he won't be here until 3.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: We won't infringe his human rights.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: May I raise one further matter while we're waiting?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, that relates to what happened last Friday with Mrs. Kovacevic, when -- and I was actually watching, although I wasn't in court, when she arrived with this CD. Your Honour, I have to tell Your Honour that no notification whatsoever was given to us in advance that she was going to be producing effectively this series of documents. Now, Your Honour, accepting, although I find it perhaps difficult to believe that there wasn't some discussion about the nature of those documents before, that she brought it with her for the first time that day, she brought it at the request of Mr. Lukic, as she told Your Honours. Mr. Lukic, nor Mr. Ostojic, ever told us that she had this, that it was likely that it was going to be produced, or gave us any opportunity to look at it before it was produced. Your Honour, the Defence do have an obligation, as we did, to disclose the exhibits that they intend to use. I fully accept that occasionally, witnesses arrive with documents that the Defence haven't had a chance to see. But if that happens, it's not just politeness; it's an absolute necessity that we're told about it in advance because we may wish to object. Otherwise, what happens is you have this unseemly and time-wasting argument in court. And so, Your Honour, our request is very much this: That if there is to be any document shown to a witness or produced to a witness which we have not been supplied with, this must be done in advance of the Court hearing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Before I give you the floor, may I add that maybe we have to discuss this in the framework of a 65 ter (i) meeting, but it has also to be discussed in open court. What we experienced, not only on Friday but related to the other witnesses as well, it comes very close to that what we could call abuse of procedure because evidently, the proffers provided to us had nothing or nearly nothing to do with that what was the testimony of the witness. And I don't want to continue to be compelled to put to a witness that it was the submission of the Defence that the witness would or could give a statement, for example, on the role of Dr. Stakic in the municipality between April and September 1992, and the witness tells us: "No, nothing, impossible. I don't know anything about this." So if we would work on this basis, we could forget about the proffers, and this would not allow us at all to prepare a hearing. I can leave it open whether or not that what was contributed by Witness Kovacevic was in favour of the Defence; but indeed, it's true if it's only a document, the document has to be shown, and it was shown in the past, always before the hearing to the other party and the Bench. And when it's even more complicated on the basis of a CD-ROM, then there has to be a possibility that we can have a look on the relevance of this document, this CD-ROM, beforehand. And I don't know yet how to proceed in future that we don't have any delay based on these shortcomings by the Defence. But we can't accept this any longer. So is the Defence prepared to accept this and in future to take care that all the relevant documents they want to put to a witness or to introduce through a witness, that this is provided in due time; that is, no later, as it was the rule during the Prosecution's case, two days in advance of the hearing of a witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, absolutely. We are really doing our best. But, for example, for Witness Sivac, we received something on Saturday, and we didn't have time to give to anybody from Saturday. On top of that, our copier machine in the Defence room is not working. Our computers in the Defence room are not working. Our printer in the Defence room is not working. So our investigators are still in the field. We are still collecting some evidence. And as you know, we submitted more than 400 documents for the translation. But it happens from time to time that we collect something a day before. So just before this hearing, I kindly asked your staff to copy something for us because our photocopier machine is not working. So I apologise, and I kindly ask you to understand also the conditions in which we work. Regarding these proffers, we are aware that we have to improve the substance of the proffers, but some of the proffers were made based on the conversation of our investigators with the witness. So for the first time, sometimes, we see the witness here, and that's what happened why the protective measure was poorly explained by the Defence for the last witness, who had the protective measure. And also that's the reason why it happened that that witness knew nothing about the period which is actually indicted in the fourth amended indictment. We are aware of these mistakes of our side, and we will try during this week and during the weekend to amend our proffers for the future witnesses. And we appreciate the Chamber's patience. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. May I then just to continue -- there might be other issues -- the witnesses of this week. There would be number -- after Mr. Sivac, number 14, number 20, number 47, number 40, and there is this witness who had been heard previously. And then 58.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: 58, Your Honour, was not coming. We were just informed that he was not found. He contacted my investigators, but I don't know what was the reason of not coming. He's not coming.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: So it will be limited to four witnesses this week?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Hopefully we will be able to finish them, because those are pretty -- they will give us pretty lengthy testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: But may I ask, when we have already discussed this issue, both parties, and this is also a question of mea culpa, that we should show a little bit more self-restraint and limit us to the relevance of -- the relevant portions of the statement. So I'm afraid also when I see the proffer of today's new witness, number 041 [sic], and see that the direct examination will last approximately four to four and a half hours, and at the same time, the testimony seems to be limited to that period of time when Dr. Stakic was the director of the health centre at the hospital, I wonder how it is possible to hear a witness on this period of time not related to the fourth amended indictment for a period of more than four hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Although this witness was not directly connected with Dr. Stakic at that time, she would give some testimony regarding the time before, during, and after the indictment. So ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: So in conclusion, let's try to concentrate on the relevant issues, and maybe by doing so, being a little bit shorter as we were the last week. And also, in the direction of the Prosecution, I think it's - if not absolutely necessary and mandatory - to put to a witness once again the entire case and come back to all the former colleagues, and maybe this also could be a little bit shorter. It would help us to proceed more expeditiously, because I emphasise this, and I have to re-emphasise, there is no additional day possible. And we have to finalise the hearing by the 21st of March. Just to be on the safe side, may I ask the parties in case - I don't hope this, that it will be the case - that my health condition does not allow to continue during this week, could you agree that we continue as we did in the past in the absence of Judge Fassi Fihri, that the witnesses should not come back once again, that we take depositions by the remaining Judges? Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: We do, Your Honour. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We agree, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. Okay. Then another issue, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Another issue is that we had the obligation according to the order of this Chamber to contact six witnesses, and I would like and ask you kindly to go to the private session. Because we'll be mentioning the names.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Private session, please, or closed session.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, just two matters briefly: Just regarding the document examiner, explaining to them exactly what the task was quite complicated, because they were very concerned with exactly what they were comparing to what. And Mr. Corin coordinated with them regarding that. I understand that their report is not yet complete. I'm not sure what date that is expected.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Okay. But we can forget about this. We should also take into account the deadline here for the Defence whether or not to hear this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Yes, I believe they told him it would take a couple months, and that was before the holiday break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: But the same deadline would be true here, say, beginning of February. Otherwise, it would be too late. We can't infringe the right of the Defence when it's another expert. Here, the same time limits are applicable. It's nice to see a bundle of documents in a language we do not understand. We are far from the truth. And no doubt, Judge Vassylenko will understand it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: I'd like to explain about this. But I'm not proposing to offer all of these. As you may or may not recall, at the end of Mr. Sivac's testimony, he referred to one article which he had in his hotel room. Your Honour asked him to bring it back. We then went to the videolink, he left, and we never did produce that article in his hotel room. I asked him yesterday when I met with him if he had it. And to be honest right now, I'm not sure which one that was. And he brought down this group of Kozarski Vjesniks. Although I've handed out the whole bundle, I believe some of these are already in evidence. Many of them have been disclosed. I don't propose to use them all. I wanted mainly the Court and the Defence counsel to have the opportunity to put to Mr. Sivac any that they thought were relevant. I would just like to have a moment to go through it. Perhaps Your Honour would allow a short break. I'd like to go through it with one of my language people. But the specific ones I wanted to ask about if his testimony is reopened is a Kozarski Vjesnik article that dealt with - there is one in here that deals with - it's after the takeover - radicals versus the Muslims that were adopting the Gandhian way. It lists those individuals. It has pictures of Mr. Mujadzic, for example, as one of the radicals, and then it has pictures of those who were not in the Gandhian way, and it has pictures, for example, of Dr. Sadikovic and Muhamed Cehajic among those individuals. I think that that would be of some use. There's also --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I think can't we do it this way, that we leave it to the witness to tell us what from his point of view is really important, that we don't have to reopen the entire case. As I indicated earlier, the main purpose is to find out what about the discrepancies between two slightly different testimonies opposed to this, the statement of another witness heard by you in person in August last year. This should be -- we should focus on this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: I don't need to actually ask him any questions other than did he bring these documents, and those will later be translated, those the Defence select or Your Honours, and we will have the translation of the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Okay. So if the witness would be prepared, then you are prepared to start immediately?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Yes. I will only have a question about bringing the documents, and then turn him over to the Defence. I do have --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Yes, it's up to you, whether you want or not we reopen the Prosecution's case for a moment, and therefore it could be you starting with that what you heard yourself from another person in August 2002 on the basis of a video. And to have the same basis, I asked the audio unit that the video may be prepared, and I mentioned already this as an exhibit that we can immediately go medio in reas, and therefore start with the remarks on a concrete exhibit given to us previously by Mr. Sivac. This would be S52-1. If this also could be prepared at the same time, we could see also in the beginning the video. May I ask the usher to escort Mr. Sivac into the courtroom. Thank you. The Defence received this medical record for Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We brought that medical record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: But it was disclosed to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: No, I don't have that medical record. And my understanding, I wasn't quite clear, and I asked Ms. Korner, my understanding that the Court had ruled there would be no questions about it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: In principle, there's no due caution to go into these details. So therefore, I was taken by surprise. My apologies. Good afternoon, first of all. Thank you for coming once again. And as it's new testimony, may we please hear once again your solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. You may be seated. Let's hope that it will be only a very short testimony. But we thought it would be more appropriate not to run the risk that you would be called later by the one or other side, or even by the Judges, and then to have to come another time. And therefore, please understand that we took the opportunity and we are more than happy that you agreed to be here today. The floor is for the Prosecution, after we have now reopened the Prosecution's case.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Mr. Sivac, yesterday I spoke to you, and you provided me with a set of photocopies of Kozarski Vjesnik articles. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: And perhaps these originals that you provided could be handed back to the witness. They have been photocopied. Is it correct that you obtained these from another individual who told you he had received them in Sarajevo. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. This person's name is Emsud Ramolic. He's the main editor of a newspaper published in Sanski Most called Prijedorski Dnevnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Among that set of documents, first of all, in the set that Your Honours have, I ask for Your Honours' assistance how you want to handle this, because we don't think we want to translate all 28 pages. But there are 28 pages, it's possible either Your Honours or the Defence may later request translations of some of these. I don't know if you want us to mark the entire bundle as one document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I think it's the most appropriate way. I recall after --

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: 49 pages. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: You stated, and in fact I had already forgotten this, that at the end of the previous testimony, the witness told us that he had in his hotel room some additional documents and clips of newspapers, especially Kozarski Vjesnik. And if the witness could be so kind and to indicate those to us which from his perspective are relevant to that period of time, April to September 1992, related to Dr. Stakic in Kozarski Vjesnik. On a short perusal, I already found two articles on Dr. Stakic. And maybe you can limit this by just reading out these parts and portions you believe that are relevant for our case. And only this be admitted into evidence later on.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Are there any copies for the interpreters?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I think we can give two sets of copies for the interpreters, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I begin? Are there any specific questions?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: May I ask the interpreters, do they have --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: We do have our own copies of the B/C/S version, Your Honour. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: If you could be so kind and indicate to what article in Kozarski Vjesnik you want to guide us to, and that in order that the interpreters know which article this is. And then please read out this document that it need not be formally translated once again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let me tell you, there is a very peculiar edition of the Kozarski Vjesnik paper here which is dated 29th of May, 1992, which means precisely during the period while the ethnic cleansing of Kozarac was underway. The Crisis Staff of Prijedor Municipality, part of which was also the secretariat for information, prepared the Serbian people, the Serbian army, and the Serbian police for the carrying out of the ethnic cleansing of the town of Prijedor. Just before the start of the ethnic cleansing of Prijedor itself, in Kozarski Vjesnik, articles appeared that I had spoken about which, in a very dirty way falsified the biographies of many very prominent and well-respected citizens of Prijedor. And all the people accused on the pages of this newspaper at that time left without a right to defend themselves, to speak up for themselves were marked off to be killed and were later to be killed at one of the camps, either Omarska or Keraterm. As you see, the article is called Ratni Dnevnik war diary, the secretariat for information. In all these articles, not a single article is signed. We don't have the author's name. It is merely stated that the articles were written by the secretariat for information. And if I may elucidate, that secretariat, Milan Korijalic worked there, a former journalist for a newspaper called Informacije, which was published by the Ljubija iron ore mine. And all these articles were written I think by the same hand and if I may say, the same head. They were conceived in the Crisis Staff itself, and the so-called unit of the secretariat for information headed by Milan Korijalic. Preparation to begin ethnic cleansing. And I guarantee you that it was precisely these articles here, criminal of a general nature, these articles were used to sling mud on the reputation of Mirza Mujadzic. And then you have a pamphlet here, a war commissioned by Zagreb, and then the next headline reads: "Kozarac taken." I'm not sure what this means, who it is supposed to be taken by. And then you have another article accusing the Muslims that they were holding their own people hostage and that they tried to kill their own people. That sort of thing. You see, this particular issue of Kozarski Vjesnik can show you in quite graphic terms that whatever happened in Prijedor a day or two -- one or two days after the 30th, the 30th is when, as I said, an attempt to liberate Prijedor from Slavko Ecimovic and his group took place. But it was sham. And it had been commissioned to serve as merely a good cause, a motive, for the Serbian authorities in Prijedor to start their ethnic cleansing campaign in Prijedor itself. And that's exactly what happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: There are a couple of specific articles I would like you to direct your attention to. Can you find the issue dated 28th of May, and in the upper right, there's the lily symbol appearing. If you look at what I'm holding in my hand, this is what I'm ...

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: That is actually page 4 of the issue of the 28th of May.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Yes. Just so all Your Honours and Defence counsel sees the page I'm looking at. This is page 4 of the 28th of May. Excuse me. It's 1993. It is dated 1993.

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I have it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: In this issue dated 1993, can you just read the headline for us.

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the headline, this is one of the series of articles by Rade Mutic and Zivko Ecim, and the headline is -- I'll try to be specific -- "one year after the attack on Prijedor," and then it continues, "Bosnia, Bosnia, Uber Alis." And the main headline: "What our sovereign neighbours had in store for us." This is a pamphlet, Mr. President, Your Honours, in which the blame for everything happening in Prijedor day in and day out is shifted to Bosniaks, Muslims, and Croats.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: On this page 4, if you're looking at the same article I am, there are eight photographs, two groups of four. Can you explain how the article groups these eight individuals.

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you see, this strikes me as very interesting. The first group, the group higher up on the page, there's a caption that reads: "These are the advocates of the peaceful way of solving the Prijedor crisis." And their names are: Professor Muhamed Cehajic, president of municipality; Dedo Crnalic, well-respected businessman from Prijedor; Nedzad Seric, president of the Prijedor court, and Mr. Camil Pezo, a businessman and head of an organisation of labour based in Prijedor. Even according to the journalists of Kozarski Vjesnik, they were considered to be in favour of a peaceful solution. And yet, they were all to one killed in the Omarska camp. Whereas the so-called militant group, as they were described here, those favouring the war option, included Dr. Mirza Mujadzic, Hilmo Hopovac, Elvedin Rizvan, and Kemal Alagic, the wild one. They are still alive. They live somewhere in Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you. If you can turn to the next page, page 5, there's an article that includes a number of signatures, 46 signatures. Can you read the headline of that article.

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The pros and cons of Gandhi and resistance." What was debated at the meeting of the democratic action party held in Hambarine on the 10th of May.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: And this is regarding the meeting on the 10th of May, 1992, that they are reporting on a year later. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this was written one year later.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: And who is -- does the article explain was the leader of this group that sought to pursue the Gandhian way?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's clear from the article that it's Dr. Eso Sadikovic. He said our view is to keep peace, to keep peace as long as possible. That's what Dr. Eso Sadikovic said. Ghandian resistance can be a double-edged sword, Islam Bahonjic retorted.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Sivac. There are some photographs that are very dark on our copy and your copy, but the photograph on the left of these three individuals, is that Dr. Eso Sadikovic?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, that's him. This is a photograph showing Dr. Eso Sadikovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: I don't know if this has come into evidence in this case yet. Can you tell us the ethnicity of the wife of Dr. Eso Sadikovic?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Dr. Eso Sadikovic's wife was a Serb. Her name was Zorica. And originally, her family came from Serbia, from Valjevo, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Perhaps you can help me. There's an article in April 1992, I believe it's the 3rd of April, 1992. If you could find that issue, and there's a article discussing that the -- this is prior to the takeover, that the Serbian authorities had appointed their own government. It may be the 24th of April. I believe it's the 24th of April.

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Can you tell me what date is that -- can you tell us the date of that article, and the page. Perhaps if you put it on the ELMO and show us which article you're referring to.

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The article I'm talking about is dated 24th of April, 1992. The headline is "the political scene in Prijedor" and the headline below is "the elected government of the Serbian municipality."

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: I don't know, perhaps someone may request this to be read word for word. But this indicates that the Serbian authorities in Prijedor have appointed their own government, correct, and names the individuals that were appointed to various positions such as Milomir Stakic and Mico Kovacevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: May I ask the witness to be kind enough to read out this entire article.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "Elected government of the Serbian municipality. The assembly of the Serbian municipality of Prijedor adopted a decision to have the SDK of the Serbian municipality annexed by the service of public administration, SDK, of the autonomous region in Banja Luka. Last Thursday, on the 16th of April, at the 5th session of the assembly of the Serbian municipality of Prijedor, several important decisions were passed. First and foremost, we are referring to the election of the government for the Serbian municipality of Prijedor, as well as to the adoption of the decision on the SDK joining the Serbian municipality of Prijedor and the SDK of the autonomous region of Bosanska Krajina in Banja Luka. "In addition to the president of the Serbian municipality of Prijedor elected earlier, and the president of the Executive Board of the Serbian municipality of Prijedor, Milomir Stakic, and Mico Kovacevic, the following people were also elected members of the first government of this municipality. Bosko Mandic, as the vice-president of the executive committee; Ranko Travar, as the secretary for the economy; Boro Babic, as the director of the revenue service; Slavko Budimir, secretary for national defence; Svetozar Petrovic, secretary for general administration; Radenko Banovic, director of the municipal land survey; Vojo Pavicic, secretary for urban planning; Milovan Dragic, director of the communal utilities; Rajko Mrsic, director of the firefighters societies; Simo Drljaca, chief of the public security station; Slobodan Kuruzovic, commander of the municipal staff of the TO, Territorial Defence; Slobodan Goronjic, director of the SDK; Mico Kreca, president of the Court; Milenko Tomic, public Prosecutor;, and Dusko Milojica, as the president of the tort court. "By a unanimous decision of the deputies, and also the deputies from the so-called left bloc of the Serbian people took part in the vote, a decision was adopted to have the SDK of the Serbian Municipality of Prijedor." This is a bit unclear, I think. I think it says: "Before the problem is dealt with -- before the crisis in the republic and municipality is dealt with in a political way, enacted by the SDK of the autonomous region of Bosanska Krajina." Signed Rade Mutic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: May I take it that this article is tendered by the OTP?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We have the same objections as previously regarding Kozarski Vjesnik.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Taking into account this, admitted as the next available Prosecution document exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: S387B, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: S387B admitted into evidence, and please may it be marked that we find the translation on our today's transcript. Thank you. Then please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Could it be correct, then, Mr. Sivac, that this article indicates that Mr. Drljaca was elected at the party meeting in Prijedor of the SDS, and the article does not mention the minister of the interior?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct. It's clear if you read the article.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: If we can just move to one other short article that I noticed. If you can find the 28th of June, 1992, the front page. I would ask you to look at that, when you find it. It has a picture of a baby being held in the air.

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a moment, please. Yes, I have it here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Is there an article there about Dr. Sikora, Zeljko Sikora, that appears on the front page?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In the lower left corner, you have an article. The headline is: "A monster doctor."

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: And can you briefly summarise what the article alleges regarding Mr. -- Dr. Sikora.

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, some minutes ago, I said that Serbian political leaders, while preparing the ethnic cleansing of Prijedor, and this is further proof of that, kept falsifying the biographies of certain eminent citizens of Prijedor, especially the intellectuals. And they were biding their time so that they could kill these people when they arrested them. Again, this is a very interesting article in which Dr. Zeljko Sikora is being denigrated. He is Czech by origin, and his parents had arrived in Prijedor a long, long time ago. He was a very humanitarian person, and a doctor, a gynecologist. And for reasons unknown to me, but obviously those who wrote this article knew very well what they were after, who Zeljko Sikora was, and this was a method they choose to employ to mark him off for the kill, which was later carried out in the Omarska camp.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: May I ask you once again to be kind enough to read the entire article, because we want to refer, if necessary, to the article as such. And please understand your comments on the article are interesting, but the basis for our continuing discussion has to be, first of all, the underlying document. And therefore, please read out this article you just mentioned. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "Teachers, priests, and doctors were always particularly respected people in these areas, especially doctors. As soon as you say the word "doctor," immediately you imagine an extraordinary man who has devoted his life to sick people regardless of their skin colour, ethnicity, or religion. But not all of them are like that. There are doctors among them who have abused their white coat as a disguise in order to do things which have nothing to do with the doctors' ethics or any other kind of ethics. They used their white coat in order to commit crimes. Even among us, there are a number of such people. A doctor was arrested who, when interrogated, without a trace of remorse or compunction, admitted to his crime, adding only that he was now sorry he had started with his crimes too late. "What he did was actually more than a crime. He castrated new-born males of Serb parents. He caused women, Serb women, to abort, and he sterilised them. Is a punishment conceivable that would be sufficient to punish that kind of crime, an abominable crime to every human being? Is it blood in that man's veins, or poison? Is there an end at all to human irrationality, irrationality that wouldn't even leave those newborn children, helpless infants in peace. His church will probably forgive the crime he committed. It will probably suffice for him to just kneel down in front of the confession booth."

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Do you know the religion of Dr. Sikora, who you mentioned was of Czech ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Czech Catholic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Do you know if in Prijedor, Catholic Czechs were considered to be aligned for some reason with Croats, or were equated with Croats?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, mostly all Catholics were considered Croats and Ustasha.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: May I ask, first, we are aware that as to the fact this was a war edition of Kozarski Vjesnik, we don't have any signature on the author. But how do you come to the conclusion that this article is on Dr. Sikora? I didn't understand it. Maybe I was a little bit confused.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, Mr. President, let me tell you. In one of the later issues of Kozarski Vjesnik, I had it somewhere then, but I couldn't find it. I mean, all of this was referring precisely to Dr. Izdenko Sikora, the only gynecologist who was killed in the Omarska camp. It was him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. This, no doubt, makes sense. I think it's now the right opportunity to have a break. This will allow our witness, after this long day, to have another period of 30 minutes recreation. It will allow the Prosecution to concentrate on the remaining parts they want to introduce. This will allow Judge Vassylenko to concentrate or focus on the one or other article identified right now. And later on, we immediately will come back to the questions we had by the Defence, no doubt. The trial stays adjourned until 4.20. But may I not forget, please, Defence, to also disclose the material given to the Bench and to the Prosecution in the meantime. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Please be seated. May I ask first the Prosecution whether they want to introduce additional article, but we should not forget to give the last child a name. This was the article just read out. This would be the next exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Objections? We are aware there is no signature at all.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't have anything here.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The same objections, plus there is no author of the text.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: We are aware. Admitted into evidence, S388B. And once again, translation be found on the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you. Your Honour, I'd now like to turn to the issue dated the 29th of May, 1992. On the front page just for Your Honours and Defence counsel is a picture of people walking in Prijedor. And the articles in question would be the articles on page 2. There appear to be one, two, three, four articles signed "Crisis Staff." I leave it to Your Honours' discretion. The first, second, and third in particular, the top ones, I believe need to be read in their entirety. Either we could translate them or have the witness read them now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I would really appreciate that we can ask questions and that the witness, if he so wants, give additional comments on these articles. If he once again can be so kind and read these articles mentioned by the OTP. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The heading reads: "The Serbian government of Bosnia-Herzegovina, Autonomous Region of Krajina, municipality of Prijedor, Crisis Staff. And the title is press release. On 22nd of May at 1900 hours, paramilitary formations from the territory of the local commune Hambarine carried out an armed attack on the members of the army of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina. The attack was carried out in the following manner: The vehicle which carried the members of the military was stopped at the checkpoint manned by illegal forces situated at the outskirts of Prijedorsko Polje. Having been stopped, the members of the military were then taken out and disarmed. "Later they were fired upon from several locations. On this occasion, two members of the military were killed, and four others were severely wounded. They are currently undergoing treatment at the Banja Luka medical centre. The Crisis Staff hereby informs the public that shortly after that, an evacuation of the killed and the wounded was organised. However, members of the Muslim paramilitary formations did not allow for the wounded to be taken out, but continued with the armed operation. Since the evacuation of the members of the military was made impossible, the command has reached -- issued an order to use force in order to pull out the killed and the wounded members of the army. "This military activity was intended to issue a warning. Its purpose was not to provoke violence which shielded the perpetrators of this crime. The Crisis Staff wishes to warn that from now on, they will no longer be warning actions, but that they would engage in to direct activity on -- it would directly attack the areas where perpetrators of such acts and members of the paramilitary formations are in hiding. The Crisis Staff is hereby ordering the population of the local commune of Hambarine and other local communes in this area, that is, all residents of Muslim and other nationalities, that today, Saturday, 23rd of May, until 12.00, they must surrender the perpetrators of this crime to the public security station in Prijedor; in particular, Aziz Aliskovic and his group, which was in a most -- which is the direct and immediate organiser of this conflict. "With this crime, all deadlines and promises have been exhausted, and the Crisis Staff can no longer guarantee the security of the residents of the above-mentioned areas -- of the above-mentioned area. Signed, Crisis Staff in Prijedor, on the 23rd of May, 1992."

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Sivac. In the middle of the page, there is another box that begins -- the article begins "Krizni Stab" and is again signed and dated Prijedor, 23rd of May, 1992. Can you read that article.

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The Crisis Staff of the Prijedor Municipality, following its meeting which was held today, sometime before 1500 hours, wishes to inform the public of the following: Since we have heard nothing from the residents of the Hambarine area, and since the attackers and the killers of the soldiers who were members of the Serbian army of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina have not been surrendered, and since we have noticed regrouping of the Muslim paramilitary formations and their military activity targeted against members of the Serbian army of the Republic of -- members of the army of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, the latter were forced to retaliate. The Crisis Staff declares null and void the decision on the surrender of weapons reached on the 27th of May, 1992, with the deadline expiring at 1500 hours. The Crisis Staff is ordering an unconditional surrender of weapons and military equipment immediately at the reception point in the barracks Zarko Zgonjanin, not later than 1800 hours on the 23rd of May, 1992. "When surrendering weapons at the vehicle which will carry the illegally obtained weapons, it is necessary to put out a white flag, so that the members of the security organs are able to act in accordance with their authority and their orders. "All citizens who comply with this order and the residential areas from where the illegally obtained weapons will be returned shall be guaranteed personal and legal security as well as the security to their property. No legal measures will be taken against those persons who returned the weapons by the specified deadline. Likewise, they will be guaranteed safe return to their places of residence. Crisis Staff of the Municipality of Prijedor, 23rd of May, 1992."

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you now read the article in the box to the right, also signed at the bottom "Crisis Staff."

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Crisis Staff has obtained information to the effect that the members of the Muslim paramilitary formations Becir Medunjanin, Mirza Mujadzic, and a few other former active officers of the JNA, commanders of the Green Berets in Kozarac, order the setting on fire of the column of the Muslim people from the area of Kozarac and the surrounding areas on the Kozara mountain. This shocking news is yet another proof that the so-called leaders of the Muslim people are not only politically irresponsible, not only obsessed by its own interest, but they have also overstepped the last limit, the last line which divided them, which set them apart from -- which divided them from inhuman criminal behaviour. We hope that these events in Kotlovaca will be a clear sign to those who have so far not understood that their leaders are not leading them -- are leading them into death. The military of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina are trying -- are doing their best to put out the fire around the column of people in Kotlovaca, and to help the innocent people to save their lives. We hope that this tragic event will not serve as a motive for those who have so far attacked us, to attack us once again and to represent, to interpret, the crimes of the Muslim leaders as crimes committed by Serbian people. The Crisis Staff hereby promises that they will do their best in order to help these unfortunate people. In Prijedor, 26th of May, 1992."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: We have to mark these three articles. Objections, as usual, on the same basis? Thank you. And the next exhibit numbers would be S388C, D, and E.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will be S389-1, -2,-3B.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: This will be perhaps easier. 389-1, 2, and 3, in the order appearing in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: I'm sorry because my language abilities are extremely limited, sir, I believe the article you just read would have been in the lower right just above the name Mile Mutic. Perhaps we could put it on the ELMO and you could point to what you just read, if you could put it on the machine to your right.

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have read this article.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Now, if you could read the article above it dated the 24th of May, 1992, that actually was the one I was referring to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: This would be, then, -4.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: If you could read, sir, the article in this box, the article dated the 24th of May, 1992.

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 24th of May, 1992. Let me just find it. What article do you have in mind?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Perhaps the usher can help. On the same page, the centre box on the right-hand side. It again begins "Crisis Staff, Prijedor."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Just on the ELMO, if you can point to it on the ELMO so that also Madam Registrar can follow what now will be -4.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Perhaps if the usher could point to this article and show it to the witness. This one here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: On the ELMO, perhaps, so we are sure that everything is talking about the same article. The usher or the witness could point to the article?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's the one here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Yes, yes, correct. Yes, please read that. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Prijedor municipal Crisis Staff, at its meeting held this morning, reviewed the situation on the territory of the Prijedor Municipality and concluded that after yesterday's action carried out by the army, with the purpose of disarming Muslim paramilitary formations in the Hambarine local community, the situation calmed down during the evening hours of the day. The Crisis Staff assessed the action to have Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. been carried out successfully. During the fighting, there were no casualties sustained by the army. One member of the army was wounded; however, thanks to a rapid intervention of the medical corps, he was given adequate assistance and sent to the Banja Luka medical centre for further treatment. "In yesterday's action, the military used a small part of its capabilities. The Crisis Staff and the command of the region will continue the action of disarming of the members of the paramilitary formation until it is completed. We wish to warn that the order of deblocking all of the roads on the territory of the Prijedor municipality must be complied with, in particular, so far as it concerns the portions of the Banja Luka main road in the area between Kozarac and Omarska local communities. "Yesterday, several individuals who were involved in organising and distribution of weapons were taken to the public security station in Prijedor, including Muhamed Cehajic. The Crisis Staff wishes to inform the public that during the night, there was intermittent shooting in the outskirts of the local -- in the town itself and the surrounding local communes. During the night, there were attempts by Muslim paramilitary formations to initiate new conflicts, and the army and the police of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina retaliated -- responded to every provocation strongly. In the area of Surkovac, concentration of individuals dressed in uniforms of the army of Republic of Croatia, references to the members of the Croatian national guard, was observed. There has been movement of population from one part of the municipality to the other. Having reviewed the overall situation and the security situation in the territory of the municipality, the Crisis Staff wishes to emphasise once again the need for the residents of the local communes, where part of the paramilitary formations are located, take all the measures in order to disarm them, and that the municipality organs be handed over all illegally obtained weapons. "The Crisis Staff wishes to inform the public that a meeting with representatives of these local communes have been agreed upon; however, we also wish to inform you that there are no negotiations regarding the action of surrendering of weapons. The only thing that can be negotiated are deadlines and current problems relating to these -- to this activity. The order on disarming should be -- must be complied with until its completion. Prijedor, 24th of May, 1992."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: This article, would that be taken into account the objections by the Defence, S389-4. Admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Same objections, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Just to complete this important series, could you read the last article. I believe you have not read the one dated the 25th of May, 1992, which appears in the next line down in the centre. Again, signed Crisis Staff, dated Prijedor, 24 -- 25th May, 1992.

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have that one. Sir, I do understand what you want me to do, but I would just like to briefly comment on this. This press release by the Crisis Staff offers an excellent explanation. I was just giving you the tape where you can see actually the local commune citizens turning over their weapons at the barrier. This footage was recorded by Rade Mutic, and Zivko --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter didn't get the last name.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Who were regarding from Prijedor at that time. So should you need it, you can use this evidence in this trial.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Sir, you were referring to Zivko Ecim, and that is the tape that you provided us when you were here in July was played in court. Now if you can --

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Now if you can please read the Crisis Staff article dated the 25th of May, 1992.

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Following the attacks on Zarko Zgonjanin barracks from the Puharska village two days ago and yesterday, an attack during which the army did not return fire, the Crisis Staff of Prijedor Municipality would like to inform the public of the following: The participants in this attack are well-known. They are former police officer Senad Grozdanic, and Said Grozdanic, and Hamdija Balic with his group. At the same time as the barracks, the facilities of the electrodistribution company were attacked as well as several police checkpoints. At the same time, there was an ongoing attack by the Muslim paramilitary units -- by the Muslim paramilitary units in the villages of Kozarac and Kevljani, which clearly indicates that there was a coordinated effort, an attack, by the Green Berets, and the perpetrators and the organisers of the attack on the barracks at the request of the citizens of Puharska were erected this morning and they are currently being investigated. The citizens of Puharska confirmed on that occasion that they wished to testify before the relevant organs to the effect that the army did not return fire when Grozdanic and his group attacked, and the reason they failed to return fire was the former good neighbourly relations that they used to have. "The army adopted the few that over the following period, it can no longer tolerate such attacks, but will instead return fire. The 26th of May, 1992, Crisis Staff."

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: For Your Honour, the videotape the witness referred to earlier, if you recall when he was here, we only played the interview of Dr. Stakic, but we later played a 15-minute excerpt of that, and that's S240-1. That included people surrendering weapons.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Right. Now this concrete article, I can take it that we have the same objections as previously by the Defence. Admitted into evidence, S389-5.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Now, if everyone could get out the issue dated the 24th of July, the first page, it includes a military review and an officer walking along in a salute. While that's being -- everyone's getting that, Mr. Sivac, just to remind us all, when you testified here last summer, you told us about a day in July, late July, when 12 buses of men from the Brdo region arrived in the Omarska camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Do you recall discussing those buses and the men from Brdo coming into the Omarska camp?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, roughly, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: I'm just asking you, I haven't had a translation of this article but just the headline. Can you read the headlines of this article, everything that appears in bold print above the photograph.

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Muslim extremists in the Rizvanovici fired on the army again. Soldier Slave Panic killed." That's the main heading. "In the immediate vicinity of the mosque in Rizvanovici on Sunday, soldier Slave, son of Zivka Panic, from Mis Glava was killed. The army is preparing a cleansing operation."

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Do you recognise the soldier saluting or the officer or soldier saluting in that photograph?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can see, this is Vladimir Arsic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: And if the Defence or Your Honours want to look at it, the copy that the witness has is a much better copy of the photograph. And that could be passed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: I have no further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. Then may I just start and guide you to your former testimony. Maybe the one or other slight discrepancy with testimonies of other persons. Therefore, please, that you know what it's all about, may the witness please be shown Exhibit S15-2-1, and may it be put on the ELMO. Do you recall that during your last testimony in summer, you were asked about the visit of a delegation to Omarska. In all likelihood, in the middle of July, 1992.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: And do you remember that you were kind enough at that time to mark some special points and areas on the picture?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I do recall that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: And may I ask now that, sometimes for the one or other witness, this artificial rebuilding may be misleading. As to the fact that we have better video footage, may I ask the video unit just to start and play a video.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Stop. Please rewind. Stop. Can you identify the building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes. I can clearly see it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: May we turn once again to the picture we have on the ELMO. Can you recall the point from where the --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, Your Honour, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Sorry. The area from where the persons or the delegations entered this area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, this section here. It's roughly speaking the northern part, the northern part of the camp, the mine. This is the main gate roughly speaking. This may have been a bit too rough a description, but between this corner here and the flags is where the delegation passed. And they halted here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Do you recall where their cars stayed when they arrived?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think here, around this section I'm pointing at. This model strikes me as a bit unnatural. It's unnatural. However, here, in this section. Below -- well, actually behind, but as far as I can remember, just behind the flag poles there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: And to the best of your recollections, all the cars stayed there, or some cars entered the area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Cars drove in carrying only Simo Drljaca and Dusan Jankovic. Then there was an armoured personnel carrier at the head of the column of vehicles driving in. And they halted just behind the delegation, the delegation consisting of Zeljko Meakic and the camp personnel. The rest of them stayed here. This was a little bit less visible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: So could you please point once again to the area where you stood at that time, when the delegation arrived.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was standing, as I said, here, to the left and to the side of this fountain from which water is spouting. It's impossible to tell me now, for me to tell now how many metres exactly, but I was standing here in this section, roughly speaking. It must be this section over here, maybe these letters are a bit thicker than I originally remembered. So a bit to the left.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: So it was impossible for you to see and identify what happened on the other side of the building or at the front side of the same building. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no, this is the front side of the building as far as I remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Yes, of course. You are right. With "the front side," I wanted to express the other side, to the right-hand side. Yes, please -- not this area. Of course, you're right.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no, this. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: And just to the other side of the building, if you go to the other side, opposed to this side of the building.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Further on. You were not able to see what happened in that area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Only as far as the corner of the garage. That's as far as I could see. Behind it, I couldn't see anything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: So, yes, may I once again -- I know you already told us where the inmates were compelled to line up and sing Chetnik songs at that time. Could you please once again indicate the area where they stood and where there were lined up.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, as I've already said in my first testimony, since 8.00 in the morning Milorad Tadic, Brk, would have us line up. But in the morning he would keep changing our disposition until he found the best one, the best line up. He would line us up here in this section. Then the inmates from the garage would be brought here, and then eventually they would remain. But when the delegation arrived, at one moment he moved us over here, and I barely managed to see that another group of inmates from the white house were also lined up here in front. Finally, there was only this position. And it was in this position that we saw the police delegation from Prijedor and Banja Luka arrive.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. And can you please tell us once again where the delegation passed these inmates standing there lined up and singing Chetnik songs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] After reporting to -- after Zeljko Meakic reported to Radislav Brdjanin, the commander of the camp, he stood here. And behind him were standing the remaining members of the delegation. Zeljko Meakic, he was right here. This is where he was standing. And Mr. Radoslav Brdjanin was standing in front of everyone else, just behind Zeljko Meakic there was Simo Drljaca and the other people from the police, from the Prijedor police, together with the shift leaders and a number of guards. After they reported to Radislav Brdjanin, Radislav Brdjanin with part of the delegation went this way. And then midway to their destination, they halted, and he tried to say something. I couldn't hear anything because people were bellowing; there was a lot of noise. We had to sing all those songs and keep shouting Serbia, Serbia. And then accompanied by part of the delegation, he came here and took the entrance to the administrative building. A minor group of people I didn't recognise was led by Srdjo Srdic and Simo Miskovic. They headed this way. It was around here, well, the last ones were always at the back of the -- that group of mine from Mujo's room, there was the old Dedo Crnalic. He managed to reach the end of the gauntlet, and he raised his arm. He wanted to tell Srdjo Srdic and Simo Miskovic something. He was trying to tell them something. They paused briefly. They waved to him, and just behind Srdjo Srdic and Simo Miskovic, Milomir Stakic passed by, together with Milan Andzic, and a couple of other people I didn't know, probably from Omarska. And then they headed this way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: As regards time, was it at the same time or did the persons mentioned by you right now, did they arrive a little bit later or a little bit earlier?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, no. It was -- let me tell you how it was. The delegation headed this way, and the other group where Milomir Stakic was, they headed down this way. So they parted ways here. They split up into two groups. I'm not sure what the reason was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: So once again, from that, it already emanates that it was and it's your testimony that without any doubt, you saw at that time both Milomir Stakic and Srdjo Srdic when this -- when the delegation arrived. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes. I still say the same.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I wanted to be on the safe side. Just one final question from my side: Do you by chance know a Ms. Nada Markovska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do, closely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Can you explain this a little bit to us.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, please allow me to just add a comment about Mr. Srdjo Srdic, if you will. Mr. Srdjo Srdic, I say, "Mr.," although it's a bit difficult for me, but I'm trying to do it out of respect for this Court. He had been a dentist in Prijedor for a very long time. He was even -- he was as close to me -- he was almost a member of my family. We were on visiting terms. We used to drink together. He used to come and see my father. Srdjo Srdic showed up in Omarska on a white suit on that particular day. I know that someone who was standing behind me was sort of shoving me in the back, but we had to keep singing. So I didn't react. But when we entered the room, Bajrisa Zeljo told me: "You saw Srdjo Srdic wearing a white suit as though he was a conducter of the Viennes philharmonic orchestra." That's how he arrived in Omarska. That was a comment, along those lines. You know even in those sad days, we did have a number of anecdotes and jokes even. Let me clarify this: You asked me about Nada Markovska, I used to work with her in the security services for a long time. Her maiden name was Babic. She was married to Milorad Markovska who was my school mate and we were the same age. He was a well-known alcoholic, and he used to lazy about all the time. For a while, she used to work as a secretary for the SUP secretary, Stojan Panic, and later she was transferred to the crime squad. And in 1992, she was in the crime squad. She worked as the secretary of the head of the crime squad, Ranko Mijic. She was a very reticent person. She worked for the SUP. She had two children, and she kept struggling with her husband who was an alcoholic. And he always refused to find work. She didn't go out to the centre very often, and she had a very reticent life. I did clash with her verbally once after the Serb takeover in Prijedor. We happened to bump into each other in the centre on a Sunday. I was standing there, and she told me: "What sort of a man are you? We're not cannibals, we Serbs, you know. We don't eat people." "What happened, I asked her?" You told Medisja Sahovic was still working in the SUP after the Serbs had taken over. No one could make him sign an oath of loyalty to the Serb authorities. Everything he was being asked to do was under duress. But that he should think about it. And then he told Nada Markovska about this, and she used this opportunity to criticise me and to tell me that Serbs were no cannibals, and that I should be careful about what I was telling people. The only thing I did was I simply advised my friend to sign or not sign an oath of loyalty to the Serb authorities, to do as he chose. But everything that was done was done under duress. And very soon, I told him then this would cease to be valid.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Did you ever see or meet Nada Markovska in Omarska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the morning, when it was possible, when guards took us out, we saw this special bus carrying interrogators -- come to the camp, and we also saw Nada Markovska, Nevenka Sikman, Dara Lujic who were all administrative workers working for the security service, we saw them coming to the camp together with the investigators and going to the administration building, going upstairs in the administration building. I also saw them once when we were lined up in front of the room where I was detained. And on one occasion, we were being beaten and made to lay face down on the floor. At one point, I managed to stand up, and I saw Nada Markovska smoking a cigarette in the company of Slavica Lakic. They were playing Chetnik music very loud from this room.
